pages.text: Two friends decided to build towers with their blocks.
One tower looked taller. The other looked shorter.
They wondered, 'Which tower is really taller?'
They decided to measure using the same size blocks.
They lined up the blocks from the bottom to the top.
They counted: one, two, three, four, five blocks tall.
The other tower measured one, two, three, four blocks tall.
Now they knew for sure which tower was taller.
Measuring with equal blocks made the comparison fair.
They learned that measuring tells us exactly how tall something is.
